passage:
Dear Sarah,

I was absolutely thrilled to catch your recent feature in the Vancouver Business Journal regarding the massive expansion of your logistics firm. Seeing your name associated with such a milestone brought back wonderful memories of our time together working at the port authority back in 2021. While our careers have taken us in different directions since then—you climbing the corporate ladder in supply chain management and me settling into consulting and community work here in Victoria—I have always kept tabs on your professional journey with great admiration. It is incredible, though certainly not surprising, to see how your strategic vision has helped your company navigate the recent supply chain hurdles that have tripped up so many other regional businesses.

Reading about your new leadership role prompted me to reach out, not just to congratulate you, but to reconnect properly. Life on Vancouver Island has been treating my family wonderfully, though my schedule has become surprisingly hectic lately. Between managing my independent logistics consulting practice and volunteering with our local municipal transit advisory board, my calendar is constantly packed. In fact, I am currently preparing a keynote presentation for an upcoming municipal planning conference next month, which means my travel flexibility is quite limited until mid-September. Despite these busy weeks, staying connected with old colleagues who truly understand the complexities of our industry remains a priority for me.

I wanted to touch base because I know how isolating leadership transitions can be at your level, especially when managing rapid organizational growth. I would love to offer any informal sounding board support I can provide from an external perspective. Whether you need a neutral sounding board to talk through team structuring, vendor negotiations, or just want to grab a coffee to vent about the headaches of modern freight management, I am completely available for virtual chats anytime during the week, or over the phone during my evening walks.

Let me know if you might have some downtime next week for a quick catch-up call. We could easily chat over Zoom on Tuesday or Thursday afternoon. I would love to hear firsthand how your team is managing the new regional warehouses and catch up on personal news as well. Hope everything is running smoothly on your end, and congratulations once again on your well-deserved promotion!

Warmly,
Liam Henderson
